FEATURES OF RAISED ICP/IMPENDING HERNIATION 
• Headache, vomiting, altered LOC, visual alterations, abducens nerve palsies 
(lateral gaze palsy) 
• Cushing’s triad: Hypertension, bradycardia, irregular respiration – late 
manifestation 
• Unilateral dilated/non-reactive pupil with decreased GCS, or fixed 
constricted pupils  
• POCUS: Optic nerve sheath diameter > 5 mm 
 
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS – SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
 
Communicating hydrocephalus – meningitis (often cryptococcal), SAH, sagittal sinus 
thrombosis 
• LP/IVD with opening pressures, remove excess CSF 
Non-communicating hydrocephalus – ventricular system obstruction due to haemorrhage 
/inflammation/mass lesions (often TB) 
• Interventricular drain (IVD). NB DO NOT LP! 
Vasogenic oedema – tumour, abscess, encephalitis, demyelinating disease, trauma, 
cerebral venous thrombosis, PRES 
• May be steroid responsive (tumour, infection, inflammation) 
• Efficacy of osmotherapy may be limited due to BBB disruption 
Cytotoxic oedema – ischaemic stroke, HIE, DAI, acute hepatic failure, prolonged seizures  
• Treat underlying cause where possible 
• NOT responsive to steroids 
Interstitial oedema – obstructive hydrocephalus forces CSF into white matter 
• Treat underlying cause, EVD 
Osmotic oedema – acute hyponatraemia, rebound oedema following rapid weaning of 
hyperosmolar therapy, dialysis disequilibrium syndrome, DKA (paediatric) 
• Treat underlying cause, correct electrolytes 
Venous outflow obstruction – cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, jugular vein 
compression/thrombus, external neck compression/masses, SVC syndrome, 
thoracic/abdominal compartment syndrome  
• Treat underlying cause 
Intracranial haemorrhage – SAH, SDH, EDH, intraparenchymal, intraventricular 
• Surgical evacuation based on location/type 
Tension pneumocephalus – trauma 
• 100% oxygen, urgent neurosurgical consult 
 
RAISED INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE/IMPENDING HERNIATION

NEUROPROTECTIVE MEASURES AND SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
• Head up 30 – 45 degrees 
• MAP > 90mmHg unless ICH, then MAP > 75-80mmHg 
• Normocarbia (PCO2 34 - 40mmHg) – lower end of normal 
• Normoxia (PaO2 60 – 100mmHg) – avoid hypoxia, O2 sats target > 95% 
• Normothermia (Temp < 37.5) 
• Normoglycaemia (Blood glucose target 5 – 10 mmol/l) 
• Correct any electrolyte abnormalities 
• Monitor for seizures – Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV, max rate 50mg/min loading dose in 
traumatic ICH 
• Sedation and analgesia to avoid coughing – coughing/gagging raises ICP 
• Consider Fentanyl 1 – 3 mcg/kg over 60 seconds, 3 minutes prior to intubation as premed 
to blunt intubation response 
• Avoid neck pressure – C-spine collars, tight ETT tape, CVP in IJV 
• Avoid excessive PEEP and elevated airway pressures 
• Avoid raised thoracic/abdominal compartment pressures 
• No role for steroids in traumatic ICH 
• Consider Dexamethasone 6 – 12mg IV tds in tumours/bacterial meningitis/other 
vasogenic oedema 
RAISED INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE/IMPENDING HERNIATION cnt. 
  
 
OSMOTHERAPY 
 
• Hypertonic sodium bicarbonate 
o 50ml of 1mEq/ml 
o Same tonicity as “6% saline 
o 100 – 150ml as emergent therapy (adult) 
 
• Hypertonic saline 
o 3ml/kg 5% OR 5ml/kg 3% 
o Central line not required 
o Monitor sodium, avoid hypernatraemia > 155 
o Avoid NAGMA/hyperchloraemia – convert to 
hypertonic bicarbonate therapy 
o Avoid increasing Na by more than 6 – 8 
mmol/day 
o Less adverse effects than mannitol 
o Bolus preferred over continuous infusion 
 
• Mannitol (less preferred) 
o 1.5 – 2g/kg over 30 – 60 minutes 
o 20% solution i.e. 100g in 500 ml 
o Large peripheral/central line 
o Complications: nephrotoxic, may induce 
diuresis, decrease cerebral perfusion, 
hypotension, electrolyte derangement, 
rebound raised ICP as mannitol crosses the 
BBB 
 
NEUROSURGICAL INTERVENTIONS 
• Tumour resection 
• Haemorrhage evacuation/Burr holes 
• External ventricular drain (EVD) placement 
• Shunt placement 
• Decompressive hemicraniectomy
